en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Twenty-Second Chapter
The Discussion on the Indeterminate:
Is all the mind of one who has fallen asleep indeterminate? Yes.
“Does one kill a living being in a dream?
“Yes.
If one were to kill a living being in a dream, then indeed, it should not be said—
“The mind of one who has gone to sleep is indeterminate.
[If it were so,] one might take what is not given through a dream...
or speak falsely.
One might speak maliciously,
one might speak harshly,
or one might utter idle chatter.
One might break into a house,
carry off plunder,
or commit robbery.
He might stand in ambush,
he might commit adultery,
or he might commit a robbery.
One might commit the destruction of a town,
one might engage in sexual intercourse even in a dream,
or semen might be emitted while dreaming.
One might give a gift in a dream;
one might give a robe;
one might give almsfood.
One should provide lodging,
one should provide medicinal requisites for the sick,
and one should provide solid food.
One should give food,
one should give drink,
and one should pay homage to the shrine.
One might offer a garland at a cetiya,
offer incense,
or offer ointment … [and so forth] …
"Should one perform a circumambulation of a cetiya while dreaming?
"Yes.
"If, then, one were to perform a circumambulation of a cetiya in a dream, surely it should not be said—"
“Every mind of one who has gone to sleep is indeterminate.
Should it not be said that “every mind of one who has gone to sleep is indeterminate”?
“Yes.
“But has it not been stated by the Blessed One that the mind of one who has gone to sleep is ‘not reckoned’?
“Yes.”
If it has been stated by the Blessed One that the mind of one who has fallen asleep is not included [within the categories of wholesome or unwholesome], then indeed, sir, you must say:
"All the mind of one who has fallen asleep is indeterminate.
The Discussion on the Indeterminate is finished.
